The price implies owner cash flow decaying ~9%/yr through years 3-5; my evidence supports roughly flat over that window before a genuine fade.

## SECTION 1 — MACRO
From DATA 1.5 / 1.6 [Actual]: rf (10y nominal) 5.24%, real 2.88%, breakeven 2.36%; COE ANCHOR 8.11% (sector loading 0.687x on a 4.17% market-consistent premium); long-run nominal growth anchor 3.75%; curve +0.45% and steepening; IG spread 1.49%, HY OAS 3.24%. Regime vector (2026-09-01): goldilocks 0.302 / reflation 0.236 / tightening 0.176 / stagflation 0.167 / recession 0.118 — contested, headline goldilocks. CPI YoY 3.35%, PCE 3.42% (2026-10-04). Active shock: `oil_shock` severity 1 (Strait of Hormuz closure, Saudi pipeline attack, China fuel-export suspension).

**Exposure:** BCRX is a US rare-disease pharma with ~all revenue in US Orladeyo plus RAPIVAB — demand is payer-driven and largely inflation-insulated (orphan pricing), so the oil shock transmits only through cost of goods/logistics (COGS was just $3.8M on $218.3M Q2 revenue, PRIMARY P1) and through the discount rate. The high-rate regime matters twice: (1) it holds my COE at 8.11% with no size premium relief, and (2) it raises the cost of the company's own $395.4M Blackstone term loan (H1 2026 interest expense $41.5M on ~$822M of debt + royalty obligation, PRIMARY P1) — a real drag that is already in my cash-flow base. A tightening regime (p=0.176) would hit a 13.75%-short name hardest; the Bear case carries +150bp on the discount rate for exactly this.

## SECTION 2 — BUSINESS & MOAT
**Engine decomposition (mandate 1):**
- **Engine A — Orladeyo US (transactional deliveries, dominant):** $625–645M FY2026 guide [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. Q2 2026: $158.2M (+1% y/y; +10% ex-EU), H1 $306.5M (PRIMARY P1). >$2B cumulative US revenue since 2020 approval (StockTwits/Yahoo, 2026-09-09) [Unconfirmed, plausible]. This is a volume-driven oral prophylactic franchise with ~97% gross margin on product sales (COGS $9.2M vs $374.7M H1 revenue, PRIMARY P1). Not an annuity — no contracted backlog exists; the "installed base" is a treated-patient fleet with switching costs only of adherence/prior-authorization inertia, not contracts. I credit no multi-year annuity because the filings show none (mandate 2: no backlog figure to cite).
- **Engine B — RAPIVAB (peramivir):** small, legacy, included in total-revenue guide; immaterial to value.
- **Engine C — Navenibart (strategic optionality):** Phase 3 ALPHA-ORBIT enrollment completed June 2026, top-line both doses Q3 2027 [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. Acquired via Astria deal closed Jan 23, 2026 (~$700M net; $400M Blackstone term loan + equity, TipRanks 2026-01-23) [Estimate]. It is a *second HAE drug* — the hedge lives in the same competitive field as the threat.
- **Engine D — M&A / external innovation:** CEO Gayer (since Jan 2026) has shut internal discovery, closed Birmingham by end-2026, cut non-GAAP opex guide to $420–440M, and stated intent to buy rare-disease assets with the ~$352.6M cash + investments on hand (PRIMARY P1; CNBC via Yahoo 2026-08-28) [Actual for guidance; Unconfirmed for targets]. This is real optionality but unmonetized — I value it only as a floor-protection effect in the Bull, not in Base.
- **One-offs to strip:** $55.7M navenibart EU license upfront inside the raised FY26 total-revenue guide (one-time); $697.8M non-cash acquired IPR&D charge in H1 2026 (PRIMARY P1); Q4 2025's $407M revenue / $246M net income quarter contains EU-sale and milestone items (DATA 4) [Actual, composition partly Unconfirmed].

**Owner earnings after SBC (mandate 2):** SBC is a real cost counted ONCE — `sbc_treatment = deducted_in_cf` (it is already expensed in GAAP net income; FY2025 SBC $85.1M, H1 2026 $30.7M, PRIMARY P1/P3). ## SECTION 9 — RED TEAM
**Strongest short thesis:** "Orladeyo is a $635M product whose entire value rests on a 44%-efficacy capsule, about to face a once-daily pill that matches Takhzyro (87%) with better tolerability. RBC models the terminal at $400–450M — that's a -30% revenue step from guide, and at ~50% operating margin that's ~$160M of EBITDA gone, which is most of this company. Meanwhile the 'hedge' (navenibart) is another HAE drug in the same fight, data not due until Q3 2027, and the balance sheet has negative equity with $822M of debt-like obligations. At $8.17 you own a declining franchise with a binary option on top."
**My answer:** (1) Timing — NDA H1 2027 means no legal US erosion before late 2027/2028; the price implies -8.8%/yr decay *starting now*, which is impossible on the regulatory calendar alone. (2) Magnitude — RBC's $400–450M is a *long-term* view, not a year-3 level; my Base holds ~$600M through FY2028 and fades to ~$520M by FY2030, which still values the equity above the price. (3) Pockets — pediatric (pellets shipping since Aug 3, 2026, PRIMARY P1), Japan (pediatric approval 2026-08-25) and RAPIVAB are revenue the adult pill does not touch in the fade window. (4) The hedge is real even if same-field: a long-acting SC every 3–6 months (PRIMARY P1) competes on adherence, where daily pills lose patients. (5) The debt is manageable today — Q2 interest of $21.7M against $98.5M of GAAP operating profit (PRIMARY P1) — and the Bear case already prices a +150bp spread shock. What I concede: if navenibart fails AND payers act fast, the short is right and the stock goes to $6.23 or lower; that is why the position is capped at 4% and staged.
